blockers: (a) FULL-SRC CHARS FAILS AS WRITTEN: the v2 notes-app transcribed faithfully from D1's sketch (permissions on every op + authenticate/principal in app.ts, ok/err/domainError outcome plumbing in execute, NoteStorage.operations.get effect refs, hand-rolled port + adapter with ok() wrapping, mode:, features: re-listed in createHttpHandler) measures 4,139 chars / 120 LOC / 4 files vs Express 3,118 / 106 / 5 — 1.33x Express. Better than v1's 1.9x (5,933 / 232 / 6, and v1 has NO http layer), but it misses D6's own 'source <= Express arm' target.

(b) WRITES PER NEW ENDPOINT FAILS AS WRITTEN: 'add notes.delete' under D1-as-sketched = 3 writes — features/notes.ts (new NoteStorage delete port op + the operation), app.ts (adapter must implement the new port op AND authenticate must grant 'notes:delete' or every request 403s), notes.test.ts. That ties Express (service/app/test = 3) and misses D6's '<=2 writes per new endpoint'. Structural cause: any endpoint needing a new effect forces a port-op + adapter-impl pair split across two files, and mandatory permissions couple the feature file to the app.ts principal list (a silent-403 drift trap for agents).

INTERNAL CONTRADICTION in the design doc: line 64 shows createHttpHandler({ application, features: [notes], authenticate }) while D3 line 106 says 'createHttpHandler({features}) needs no route list' — the features re-list is exactly the kind of duplicated registration D1 claims to kill.

(c) reads: v2-as-written already wins on read COUNT (3 files vs Express 4, NestJS 4-5, v1 5) but not clearly on read CHARS (v2 feature file is dense); only the amendments make the read win unambiguous (2 files, app.ts safely unread).
amendments: A1 Plain-value effect chain: adapters return plain values (or throw); effects.x(...) resolves to the plain output; execute returns the output value or fail(code, details) where fail is injected and typed against the op's errors map. ok/err/domainError/DispatchResult leave the app-author surface entirely (stay internal). This alone cut the two execute bodies from 11 lines of unwrap ceremony to 4 lines.

A2 permissions OPTIONAL (absent = no check) and createHttpHandler must work with zero auth config (anonymous principal); authenticate is opt-in. Removes ~230 chars of principal/authenticate ceremony from the smallest app and kills the feature-file<->app.ts permission-drift 403 trap when adding an op.

A3 port.store(name, schema): CRUD port preset shipping get/save/delete/list ops AND a built-in NoteStorage.memory() adapter. This is the single change that achieves '<=2 writes per endpoint': notes.delete no longer touches app.ts because the delete port op and its impl already exist. Also collapses the hand-written port decl + adapter block (~430 chars) to two short lines.
A4 Port ops addressable as NoteStorage.get, not NoteStorage.operations.get (collision-check reserved keys at port() build time).
A5 createHttpHandler(app) — derive routes from the app's features; delete the features: parameter from the D1 sketch (also resolves the D3 contradiction).
A6 mode optional, defaulting from NODE_ENV (test runners get dev-grade validation for free; app.ts never mentions mode).

A7 Declare HTTP status with the error, once: errors: { NOTE_NOT_FOUND: { http: 404, details: {...} } } instead of parallel errors + http.errorStatus maps — each error code currently appears 3x per operation (errors key, errorStatus key, fail call); this makes it 2x and removes the 'code has no status mapping' undefined-behavior hole.
A8 s.string({ trim: true }) transform support so normalization is declarative (zod-parity; otherwise every execute carries .trim() plumbing).

A9 app.dispatch(id, input) -> Promise<Outcome> directly ({ok:true,value}|{ok:false,error}); the kind/DispatchResult envelope moves behind an opts.detailed flag or trace mode. Kills the unwrap() helper that v1's system.ts (6 lines) and every test had to write.

A10 Fix D6's metric definition: 'source <= Express arm' must count everything the author owns (index.ts + tests included) and specify like-for-like test scope — the v2 HTTP-status-asserting test is 221 chars bigger than the Express service-only test while covering strictly more; the benchmark should either credit that or compare service-level tests. WITH A1-A9 the measured result is: v2 amended = 2,974 chars / 90 LOC / 4 files (like-for-like test) or 3,195 / 96 with the richer HTTP-status test, vs Express 3,118 / 106 / 5 — chars WIN (like-for-like), LOC WIN either way; notes.delete = 2 writes (features/notes.ts + notes.test.ts, app.ts untouched and unread) vs Express 3 writes / 4 reads, NestJS 3 writes / 4-5 reads, v1 5 writes / 5 reads. All three criteria (a)(b)(c) pass only with these amendments; as-drafted the design ties Express at best.
